    Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

    It has been revealed that creators use Kit's first-party apps and integrations to connect Kit to the rest of their business. Today we build and maintain these apps by hand, with help from an agency partner. That doesn't scale. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer II to own app delivery and maintenance end to end, so a small team can support creators of every size.

    In a recent development, you'll be the first engineer on the Apps squad. Your focus is shipping high quality apps at a high pace, and maintaining them to an industry-best standard. To get there, you'll take a systems-level view and build on Kit's coding agent. You'll work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad, which builds the coding agent. You'll own the creator experience of every app you build, and you're free to improve Kit's platform when that makes those apps better.

    This is a full-time IC role for an AI-first, product-minded, full-stack engineer who has shipped agent workflows to production and judges them by reliable outcomes, not lines of code. You combine technical depth with leadership and extreme ownership. You take input from Partnerships, Product, and Design to help shape the "what," and you own the "how." You thrive in ambiguity, take initiative without waiting for permission, and elevate everyone around you through your generosity and optimism.

    We're excited about first-party apps because they let creators do more with Kit than Kit does on its own. Our own apps should just work, and set the bar for every app built on Kit.

    Industry observers note that you'll report to John Bohannon, Senior Engineering Manager for the Ecosystem and Apps squads. You'll collaborate closely with a Partnerships Manager, Product Manager, Product Designer, and engineers on the Ecosystem squad. You'll also work closely with our AI Developer Experience squad on Kit's coding agent, and with a contractor who helps maintain our apps.

    It has been revealed that the Apps squad works as a sibling to Ecosystem. You'll set its rhythms, collaborate with our Partnerships Manager on which apps to build next, and join Ecosystem's cycle planning.

    A peer onboarding buddy will help you learn our systems and codebase, and you'll have engineers across Kit for support and mentorship.

    First Week: Set up your local environment and merge your first production code. Meet the team through Get To Know You's. Start the app handover with the contractor who maintains them today. Watch the recorded app walkthroughs and read the runbooks for our most-used apps.

    Industry observers note that first Month: Audit our first-party apps and integrations, starting with the apps that need the most maintenance. Measure what each app costs to maintain, including partner app reviews like those at Google, Meta, and Shopify. Learn how Kit's API, OAuth, and App Store support creators from small to large. Fix bugs and support escalations in the apps you now own. Learn how Kit's coding agent works with the AI Developer Experience squad.

    Recent findings suggest that first Three Months: Adapt Kit's coding agent to build your first apps and maintain existing ones. Give it the context, guardrails, and evals it needs. Turn what you learn into shared pieces every app can use, like a reusable load test, infrastructure automation, and app manifests. Write runbooks that let others work on any app. Drive each app's maintenance toward zero human time with the coding agent.

    First Six Months: Ship new apps at a steady pace. Take over the rest of the app catalog and apply the coding agent to its maintenance. Show that one engineer with agents can maintain many apps at high quality. Define the metrics and dashboards for agent-built apps: releases, reliability, time to fix, and revenue impact. Share how agents build and maintain our apps, for example in a Lunch & Learn.

    First Year: Kit ships more high-quality apps, faster, and the coding agent handles more of the routine builds and fixes, with you steering the system. The legacy integration model is retired. You use catalog metrics to recommend where the Apps squad invests next. You and the AI Developer Experience squad improve the coding agent together, so other Kit engineers benefit too.

    Expert in agentic AI development. You've built agent workflows that ship and maintain production code, with evals, guardrails, and human review.

    It has been revealed that strong in APIs, including OAuth, webhooks, and integrations with third-party platforms. Fluent in Ruby on Rails, or able to ramp into it fast. Full-stack, with React where an app needs it.

    Industry observers note that ship well-tested, performant, accessible code, whether you or an agent writes it. Set the quality bar and build the tests, evals, and reviews that hold agents to it.

    Set up dashboards, alerts, and load tests that find problems across many apps early.

    Measure each app's maintenance cost, and make the team's open capacity for fresh apps easy to see.

    Communicate clearly across Engineering, Product, Design, and Partnerships.

    Align others on goals, trade-offs, and success criteria without formal authority.

    Led a major cross-team initiative from ambiguous requirements to delivery, partnering with senior leaders across functions, with measurable business impact.

    Built agents or tools that measurably improved how a team ships software, not only how much code it writes.

    Took ownership of a codebase someone else built, with thin documentation, and made it maintainable.

    Independently managed a large project, such as a migration or deprecation that required customers or partners to move.

    Create leverage, not only features. Invest in reusable systems that make your team and others faster.

    Sources indicate that judge AI work by outcomes, like rolls out and reliability, not by the volume of code or PRs. Share what works and what the risks are.

    Own everything you and your agents produce, from code to PR descriptions. Know the details well enough to stand behind every line, and don't leave reviewers or readers to do the work.

    Lead work without waiting for a formal role or permission.

    Make reversible product decisions on your own, and know when to pull in cross-functional stakeholders like Product, Design, Partnerships, and Support.

    Break big, ambiguous problems into steps that you and others can deliver.

    Write docs that let others work on any app, so the work doesn't depend on one person.

    Put creator outcomes ahead of features.

    In a recent development, share work in progress and the reasons behind trade-offs. Give and ask for direct feedback.

    You will stand out if you have:.

    Built AI tools that other developers use, such as MCP servers, agent skills, or eval suites.

    Built integrations with creator-economy platforms.

    Directed the work of contractors or an agency partner.

    Shared your work through talks, blog posts, or open-source contributions.

    Needing established processes, full consensus, or permission before you move forward.

    Wanting a large team of engineering peers on your own team from day one.

    Preferring to stay heads-down in code over shaping what to build with Partnerships, Product, and Design.

    Preferring greenfield work over inheriting and improving legacy code.

    Building each app by hand when a shared system could serve many.

    Measuring AI success by code volume instead of shipped, reliable apps.

    Avoiding direct feedback, whether giving or receiving it.

    Sources indicate that we're 100% remote with team members across the globe. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

    Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months.

    Head of M&A at Supabase

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • We’re looking for a Head of M&A to join our Corporate Development team and help build M&A from scratch.
    • This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We’re looking for a Head of M&A to join our Corporate Development team and help build M&A from scratch. You’ll work closely with product, engineering, finance, legal, as well as founders we might acquire, helping us build a world class M&A team.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

    Map the markets and targets that matter to Supabase's roadmap, and keep the map current.

    Decide build vs buy each quarter for key product areas, together with Product and Engineering.

    Build relationships with founders early, and convert the ones we want.

    Write the case for, price, and negotiate deals, from valuation model to term sheet to close.

    Run diligence and integration end to end alongside Engineering, People, Finance, and Legal.

    Set and own integration milestones, and track every deal against the reason we did it.

    Build automation for target discovery, relationship tracking, and diligence.

    Build the Supabase M&A muscle, and improve it after every deal.

    In a recent development, note: Supabase is here to scale revenue, not headcount. You should be as comfortable as a IC as a cross functional leader, and want to build the system, not the org chart.

    Have 7+ years of experience in M&A.

    Are comfortable in highly technical domains.

    Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences.

    Have experience in async or globally distributed teams.

    Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving rapidly.

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    It has been revealed that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the tech giant. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Recent findings suggest that supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are key to us.

    In a recent development, once a year, the entire company gathers in a fresh city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    Recent findings suggest that we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    It has been revealed that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • Recent findings suggest that we’re looking for a Product Security Engineer to join our team and help strengthen how security is built into Supabase’s products, platform, and engineering workflows as we continue to scale.
    • This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    Recent findings suggest that we’re looking for a Product Security Engineer to join our team and help strengthen how security is built into Supabase’s products, platform, and engineering workflows as we continue to scale. You’ll work closely with software engineers, infrastructure teams, and technical leadership, helping us proactively reduce risk earlier in the development lifecycle and ship securely by default.

    This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. Success in this role means improving the security posture of the product without becoming a blocker to speed, autonomy, or builder velocity.

    Identify and close gaps across application security, secure design review, and vulnerability management.

    Conduct threat modeling, secure design reviews, and code reviews to identify practical remediation paths.

    Partner closely with engineering teams to provide product-focused security expertise and shape a modern security program.

    Mature how we think about security in a developer-first environment, balancing pragmatism with strong technical judgment.

    Distinguish between theoretical risk and material business risk to prioritize security efforts effectively.

    Improve security posture through scalable mechanisms like tooling, automation, secure defaults, and developer-friendly guardrails.

    Support security incident response by helping triage, investigate, and coordinate remediation for product and platform security issues.

    Participate in security on-call rotations, helping respond to urgent security events with clear judgment and calm execution.

    Help manage and mature our bug bounty and vulnerability disclosure processes, including triage, validation, prioritization, and coordination with engineering teams.

    Have strong experience in product security, application security, or security engineering.

    Are comfortable working with cloud-native, developer tools, SaaS, platform, or infrastructure products.

    Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, especially in a written, asynchronous environment.

    Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers and navigating ambiguity while moving rapidly.

    Possess a deep understanding of application security fundamentals, including auth, session management, APIs, and secrets handling.

    Have experience with vulnerability triage, bug bounty programs, responsible disclosure, or security incident response.

    Are comfortable participating in potential security on-call rotation and can balance urgency, risk, and practical remediation.

    Have experience with or interest in Postgres, Kubernetes, or building security guardrails that enable rather than enforce.

    According to recent reports, we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the organization. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    In a recent development, supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    Recent findings suggest that once a year, the entire manufacturer gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    According to recent reports, we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Industry observers note that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
